The popup dispatches browser-sidebar-comment-overlay-submit with browserTabId, conversationId, sessionId, body, attachedImages and designChange; cropScreenshotToRegion and submitDirectly are conditional. Renderer bridge invokes codex_desktop:message-from-view. Main routes through BrowserHostManager.handleCommentOverlaySubmit to comments.handleOverlaySubmit.

The create/design saved branch constructs the comment, updates threadState.snapshot.comments, dismisses the editor, syncs the comment snapshot, then awaits captureSavedCommentScreenshot using that thread page view.webContents. createdAt is comment creation time.

dismiss calls overlayManager.dismiss and closeRuntimeEditor. Overlay dismissal hides the popup BrowserWindow through UU. closeRuntimeEditor sends browser-sidebar-runtime-close-editor to the page. The page preload clears editing state inside React flushSync.

captureSavedCommentScreenshot sends browser-sidebar-runtime-prepare-comment-screenshot(commentId) to that same page. Page preload sets screenshot comment state. Its React effect waits one requestAnimationFrame before sending browser-sidebar-runtime-comment-screenshot-ready with live annotationViewportRect, markerViewportPoint and optional skipScreenshotCapture. Main waiter is keyed by webContents.id and commentId, with a 1000 ms timeout.

After readiness, captureBrowserScreenshot calls await pageWebContents.capturePage() with zero arguments, then vW and yW. The input page is the existing thread page webContents from page.view; this capture path creates no second browser or reconstructed DOM screenshot.

vW optionally calls NativeImage.crop through kCe and lW, then bW resizes while preserving aspect ratio. lW maps CSS crop coordinates with actual imageWidth/viewportWidth and imageHeight/viewportHeight; starts use floor, ends ceil, bounds clamp. yW reads getSize() and calls toDataURL(). Normal crop padding is 32, compact padding 16; maximum long edges are full viewport 1280, normal crop 1024 and compact 768.

captureSavedCommentScreenshot finds the saved comment by id, captures, then maps screenshot onto that same comment id and syncs its snapshot; finally it clears screenshot rendering state in the live page. A missing ready/image leaves the saved textual comment. This source assigns the screenshot object rather than writing a screenshot file in this method.

Shared Ca/Ta convert a comment screenshot into localBrowserScreenshot on a comment attachment. For chat input composition, tle reads comment text, uE builds browser/element context and Comment text, and sE adds the Browser comments section. Rce reads each attachment localBrowserScreenshot and adds a screenshot description text plus LT(dataUrl); zce includes those image items. pE combines the main input with zce output, and the turn request receives T.input. These are inspected serialization paths; no real comment/message or model request was submitted in this refresh.

The native main process owns the exact embedded page webContents and requests pixels from it programmatically. Its source-level capture path avoids a system screen-sharing picker and separately opened Chrome. This does not establish arbitrary external Safari/Chrome/Firefox tab access, nor runtime behavior while the app is hidden/minimized or the media is throttled; those states were not exercised.

Batch annotation flow defaults to saved submission and persistent comments; quick flow defaults to direct submission and nonpersistent comments. Saved submission stores the screenshot for later chat composition. The direct branch captures first, checks that page/thread ownership still matches, then emits browser-sidebar-direct-comment to the owner renderer.
